style: Say playfully and naturally, like a quick-witted eighth grader telling a friend about her day
lines: Hi, I'm Lucia. Every graph here tells a story. Tap the graph that tells mine. One of them is a trap.
Happy with that one? Press Choose this graph.
Yes, that graph tells it.
That's the trap. Read what that graph says, then press Tag the pieces.
Now tag each piece. Tap Up, Down or Flat, then Straight, Getting steeper or Getting flatter.
Every piece has a tag. Press Check.
All right.
Some tags are off. Fix the pieces with an X, then press Check again.
Tags shown.
Press Next story when you're ready.
I added a bonus story at the end of the set.
Your turn to draw. Read the story, then tap the grid to place points from left to right.
To curve a piece, tap its number, then tap Getting steeper or Getting flatter.
When your graph tells the whole story, press Check.
Time only goes forward. Place the next point to the right.
Your graph tells my story. Watch it play back.
Not yet. Compare each line of the story with what your graph says, then fix it and press Check.
Here's one graph that works. Yours is faint behind it.
Free draw. Place points from left to right, and I'll tell the story your graph tells.
A steady story is two numbers: where it starts and how fast it changes. Type them in the boxes, then press Check.
Both numbers are right. Now tap what each one means in the story.
Not yet. Read the note, fix your numbers, then press Check.
Here's the model. Now tap what each number means.
That's what it means.
Not that one. The right meaning has the check.
That's the whole set. Your marks are in the dots.
